area.title: Journey flow, step order and what applies when
area.scope: How the notification journey hangs together across pages: the version mount and session, the step order and next-page rules, the opening run, change and return contexts (from hub, from review, from template review), the shared journey buttons and their actions, the status strip and reference, the obligations and scope rules saying which questions apply to which consignment and what is optional versus a hard stop, the end-to-end journeys walked whole, the prototype's route and coverage tables, and the decisions ledger. Stops at any one page's own content.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. The prototype decides look and feel only (content, wording, layout, components, question order); it never decides architecture (sets, journeys, services, URL paths, field names, data-model shape, code structure). Germinal products is a sibling set of live-animals in the animals frontend. Reference lists never wait on MDM integration; address search waits on the address lookup becoming a real feature.

The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

claims.statement: Every page title in this slice follows the pattern '<page name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: await expect(page).toHaveTitle('Commodity details - Import notification service - GOV.UK')
claims.note: Inferred from every title assertion in the three specs sharing the same suffix.

claims.statement: A validation failure shows a GOV.UK error summary titled 'There is a problem', listing each error message as a link, in field order.
Each field in error also shows an inline GOV.UK error message under the field, with the 'Error:' prefix.
claims.quote: /** Inline error message under a field (GOV.UK "Error:" prefix). */

claims.statement: Journey pages submit through an action button group: buttons named 'action' whose value 'continue' is Save and continue, 'hub' is save and return to overview, and 'add-another' is Save and add another.

Some pages, such as the add-a-transporter pages, do not use the action button group and submit through a plain form button named by its text ('Continue', 'Save and continue', 'Cancel and return to dashboard').
claims.quote: /** The page's main form submit (pages without the action button group). */

claims.statement: Every Design Release 2.1 date picker takes dates as d/m/yyyy, with single-digit days and months allowed.
claims.quote: /** d/m/yyyy, the format every DR2.1 date picker takes, `days` from today. */

claims.statement: Date fields are MOJ date pickers: the user can type the date into the input and dismiss the calendar.
claims.quote: /** Opens the MOJ date picker input, types the date, dismisses the calendar. */

claims.statement: Port of entry and transit country (like country of origin) are bespoke type-and-pick autocompletes: options render on each keystroke, and clicking an option writes the hidden value the server reads.
claims.quote:
Bespoke type-and-pick autocompletes (country of origin, port of entry, transit
 * country). They render on each input event, so type per key, then click the
 * rendered option, which writes the hidden value the server reads.

A new notification's opening run takes 'Save and continue' through the whole notification, from the origin page to the review page, without stopping at the overview; the overview is reached only through 'Save and return to overview'.

The run is the whole
 * notification, not a first leg of it: "Save and continue" carries a new
 * notification from the origin page through to the review page in one pass,
 * and the hub is somewhere the user chooses to go through the secondary
 * "Save and return to overview" button.

claims.statement: The notification manifest declares 49 obligations, and the order they are listed in does not affect evaluation.

claims.statement: A notification holds three repeatable groups: commodity lines, animal-identifier records within each line, and accompanying documents. Groups are derived from the obligations that point at them with `within`.
claims.note: The three groups follow from the within references in lines.js (commodityLine), identifiers.js (unitRecord) and documents.js (documents).

claims.statement: A standard address block is a single answer whose stored value is a composite of name, address line 1, optional address line 2, town, optional county, postcode, country, telephone and email.

 * whose stored value is a composite `{ name, addressLine1,
 * addressLine2?, town, county?, postCode, country, telephone, email }`.

claims.statement: Validation of an address block's subfields (maximum lengths, formats, which subfields are mandatory) is outside the obligation model.
claims.quote:
* Field-level validation of the composite (max-length, formats,
 * mandatory subfields) is out of scope of the obligation model.

claims.statement: The model does not say anywhere which address subfields are mandatory or what limits they carry; that rule must live in the address pages or the address book, outside this slice.
claims.note: Looked in parties.js, misc.js, transport.js and the manifest header. Only the composite shape is stated.

A page descriptor has an `id`, a `slug` and page-owned `collects`. The same identity
is used by dispatch, gates and navigation.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: shared code is a library that never discovers features or imports a set; set and journey policy is supplied through explicit configuration.
claims.quote:
## Shared code is a library

Controllers call small functions from `shared/`, `lib/`, `engine/` and `flow/`.
Those modules do not discover features or import a set.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: the model decides what is in scope and whether it is mandatory or optional; the journey decides page order; task rows decide grouping on the task list.
claims.quote:
## The model owns applicability; the journey owns sequence

The obligation evaluator decides what is in scope and whether it is mandatory or
optional. Journey sections decide page order. Task rows decide how work is grouped
on a hub.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: page and section gates are derived by default from page ownership, scope and prerequisites; an authored gate is reserved for policy the derived rule cannot express.
claims.quote:
## Gates are derived by default

[`src/server/app/flow/gates.js`](../flow/gates.js) derives normal page and section
gates from dispatch ownership, scope and prerequisites. Authored gates are reserved
for journey policy that the derived rule cannot represent.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: each answer is owned by exactly one page; duplicate or missing ownership is rejected, and a page claims a collection's root rather than each nested field.
claims.quote:
## One obligation has one page owner

[`src/server/app/flow/dispatch.js`](../flow/dispatch.js) rejects duplicate and
missing ownership.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: the model holds no display copy; labels, hints, options, validation messages and templates belong to the journey, and a boot-time purity check rejects display-shaped keys in the model.
claims.quote:
## The model has no display copy

Obligations contain stable domain identity, scope, mandate and invariants. Journeys
own labels, hints, options, validation messages and templates. Boot-time purity
checks reject display-shaped keys in the model.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: the bridge is the only seam between the model and the pages; a journey registers its field bindings with it.
claims.quote: ## The bridge is the model-to-page seam

claims.statement: Existing ruling: composition is explicit; only a set's own gateway knows which set and journey exist, and the model, bridge, engine and flow receive their policy keyed by set id.
claims.quote:
## Composition is explicit

A set's own gateway — today
[`routes-live-animals.js`](../routes-live-animals.js),

claims.statement: Platform limit: the obligation model is executable code (scope rules are functions), not portable JSON configuration.
claims.quote:
Obligation `applyTo` rules are JavaScript functions. Helper metadata makes their
dependencies inspectable, but the manifest is not portable JSON configuration.

claims.statement: Platform limit: a page's derived gate opens when at least one answer it collects is in scope and its prerequisites pass.
claims.quote:
The normal page gate passes when at least one collected obligation is in scope and
its prerequisites pass.

claims.statement: Platform limit: a list-valued answer (such as species) cannot drive a single-value scope gate; collection conditions use group-aware rules instead.
claims.quote:
The standard scalar gate helpers expect scalar fulfilment values. Collection
conditions use group-aware helpers and cardinality rules instead.

claims.statement: Platform limit: ownership of nested collection fields is derived from the collection root a page claims; no second page may own a nested field.
claims.quote: Do not declare a second page owner for a nested leaf.

claims.statement: Platform limit: saving is not transactional across backend projections; a partial failure is reported to the user as a recoverable backend error.
claims.quote:
Real persistence can update
more than one backend projection, and adapter code is responsible for reporting
partial failures as recoverable backend errors.

claims.statement: Field and collection names must not contain a dot or square brackets; the service refuses to start otherwise.
claims.quote:
They must be path-safe — no `.`, `[` or `]` — or `buildDispatch` throws at
  boot

claims.note: Inferred from the 'system' feature having no page. The obligation outside this slice (obligations/sections/system.js) confirms it is system-assigned at notification creation in the form GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX.

claims.statement: The animals journey's requests are tagged with these endpoint names: animals-origin, animals-commodities (and -search), animals-consignment-details, animals-identification, animals-import-reason, animals-additional-details, animals-documents (-upload, -status), animals-addresses with animals-party-picker (and -search), animals-cph-number, animals-port-of-entry, animals-transit-countries (-add), animals-transporters, animals-contact, each page with a -save.

The pages every journey shares are tagged animals-dashboard, animals-dashboard-search, animals-create, animals-hub, animals-notification-view, animals-declaration, animals-declaration-save, animals-amend, animals-cancel-amend and animals-cancel-amend-save, and the backend calls animals-backend-fulfilments, animals-backend-list and animals-backend-replace.
claims.quote:
dashboard: `${prefix}-dashboard`,
  dashboardSearch: `${prefix}-dashboard-search`,
  create: `${prefix}-create`,
  hub: `${prefix}-hub`,

claims.statement: The suite asserts no page heading, caption, label copy or error message on any live-animals page; its only text check is that the dashboard search page contains the reference number.
The suite never shows a validation error path: it only posts answers that pass, so no live-animals validation rule or error message is exercised.

Before submission the suite reopens and resaves pages already answered, cycling through origin, import-reason, additional-details, cph-number and port-of-entry for as many re-edits as it needs to reach its pages-per-notification target. A page can be reopened and saved more than once, or not at all.
claims.note: Replaces the refuted p1-064, which said all five pages are reopened every time.
